title: Tide and Orchard
premise: Ada Okafor has spent ten years ghostwriting other people's truths while hiding her own, including the anonymous letters she once wrote to a grieving stranger on a coastal island. When that stranger, Elias Mensah, moves in next door and begins writing his own memoir, Ada is hired as his ghostwriter, forcing her to sit across from the man who never knew she was his lifeline. As the last ferry of the season approaches, Ada must choose between finishing the book and vanishing, or confessing that the voice he's been searching for was hers all along. She confesses at the dock; the memoir ends with both their names, and so does the season.
about_author: Gideon Okafor is a former maritime archivist who spent years cataloguing letters recovered from coastal post offices before turning to fiction. He writes about people who love quietly and too late, and lives within earshot of a ferry terminal.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. We meet her mid-deadline, ghostwriting a celebrity chef's memoir while nursing tea in a rented island cottage. A letter arrives forwarding her old PO box mail: one of her anonymous letters returned undelivered after a decade. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: New Neighbor, Old Ink
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Elias Mensah moves into the cottage next door, carrying boxes of notebooks. Ada recognizes the handwriting from the replies she once received. He mentions hiring a writer for his memoir. Beat: dread braided with hope; she almost introduces herself and doesn't.

chapters.title: Contract of Silence
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He interviews three ghostwriters and chooses Ada without knowing why she feels familiar. The contract includes a confidentiality clause that feels, to him, like a kindness he can't name. Beat: magnetic unease; two people circling a shared past neither will name.

chapters.title: What the Ferry Took
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Through interview sessions, Elias recounts the winter his sister died and the anonymous letters that kept him alive. Ada transcribes her own words back to herself, unable to claim them. Beat: grief surfacing; intimacy built on an asymmetry only she perceives.

chapters.title: Orchard Rows
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He drags Ada to restore his sister's abandoned orchard, and working side by side, their guardedness thaws. He quotes a line from 'his' letters; Ada finishes it from memory before catching herself. Beat: warmth, then panic; the mask slips one inch.

chapters.title: The Rival's Draft
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Her celebrity client demands she abandon Elias's book, threatening to expose her ghostwriting history and destroy her career. Meanwhile Elias finds a returned envelope in her recycling, addressed in her handwriting. Beat: pressure closing in from both sides; she lies badly.

chapters.title: Low Tide Confessions
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Confronted gently, Ada admits she wrote the letters but insists it was duty, not love, and offers to withdraw from the memoir. Elias, feeling exposed by a decade of borrowed hope, lets her go. Beat: the midpoint wound; truth told too defensively becomes a lie.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A storm strands the island; the ferry schedule announces the final crossing. Ada drafts her resignation from ghostwriting entirely, while Elias rereads every reply he ever sent and realizes the woman next door answered questions no stranger could have known. Beat: reckoning; both stop running in place.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the dock, bag packed, Ada sees Elias holding the original letter she thought was lost, and reads aloud the confession she wrote into his final chapter under his name. She misses the ferry deliberately. Beat: climax; choosing visibility over safety at the exact cost of everything else.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Elias's POV, epilogue in spring. The memoir publishes with dual attribution, the rival's threat defused by Ada going independent, and the orchard bears its first fruit since Elias's sister died. They mail one more letter, signed this time. Beat: resolution; found family, honest authorship, and a whole heart lent to no one.
